name: the-red-traffic-light-closes-a-tabless-window
description: The other user-initiated close of the selected window. The red traffic light (and File > Close Window, which is the same AppKit performClose: item) reaches the window through windowShouldClose:, NOT through Widget::CloseWithReason, so it never met the user-initiated flag that Cmd+Shift+W sets - AtriumClientView::OnWindowCloseRequested is where the two routes join. Same fixture and palette gate as close-window-tabless.json, which covers the chord.

actions.note: long enough that the auto-opened palette is definitely up before the dismiss attempts
ssh-launched Atrium is not always frontmost - without this the dismiss clicks can land elsewhere
second dismiss attempt: a press on the palette's scrim, clear of the panel and the sidebar
GATE: with the palette up its scrim covers the traffic lights, so the click below would land on the scrim and measure nothing

THE MEASUREMENT: the red traffic light. The window sits at 0,30 and the titlebar band is kTitlebarHeight=40 tall with the lights centred in it, so the close button's centre is 20 in and 20 down from the window's top.
the close is posted, not run inside windowShouldClose:, so it lands a turn later

assertions.label: the-light-reached-the-window
assertions.note: separates 'the window is still standing' from 'the click missed the button' - without it a miss reads exactly like a veto

assertions.label: user-initiated-close-taken
assertions.pattern: Atrium: user-initiated close beats the last-tab-out keep-open
assertions.note: THE MEASUREMENT: the AppKit route now carries the same flag the chord sets, so the empty-strip veto steps aside for it too

assertions.label: suppression-did-not-fire
assertions.note: the keep-open veto must not have fired for this close. It still must for an automatic empty-strip close - a sibling scenario is that half.

assertions.label: browser-keep-alive-released
assertions.note: THE WINDOW IS REALLY GONE, and gone through the Browser rather than by AppKit tearing the NSWindow down behind its back - the registry only loses BROWSER when Browser::OnWindowClosing runs. vlog_after, not vlog: the same line appears at launch.

assertions.desc: LIVENESS: the app survived the close and still answers Cmd+Q, so the reentrancy of closing from inside windowShouldClose: did not leave it wedged
